step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify system participants from the visual world model and audio transcript:
   - Enterprise Users (top left actor)
   - Standard Users (bottom left actor)
   - Customer KMS Key (KMS key in customer AWS account box)
   - API Gateway (central entry point API Gateway)
   - Business Logic (compute cluster of EC2/ECS/EKS represented as ECS block)
   - Dedicated Aurora DB (top database dedicated to enterprise tenant)
   - Shared Aurora DB (middle database shared multi-tenant store)
   - Replicon Platform KMS Key (KMS key for shared database encryption)
   - I3 Fargate Service (Fargate app running Inter-Infrastructure Intelligence API)
   - I3 DynamoDB Store (DynamoDB table storing tenant routing metadata)
2. Assign valid services from vocabulary:
   - Enterprise Users -> UserCompanyWebsite
   - Standard Users -> UserConsumerWeb
   - Customer KMS Key -> KMS
   - API Gateway -> ApiGateway
   - Business Logic -> ECS
   - Dedicated Aurora DB -> Aurora
   - Shared Aurora DB -> Aurora
   - Replicon Platform KMS Key -> KMS
   - I3 Fargate Service -> Fargate
   - I3 DynamoDB Store -> DynamoDB
3. Establish logical flows:
   - Flow 0: Standard Multi-Tenant Flow (Users -> API Gateway -> Business Logic -> I3 Lookup in Fargate/DynamoDB -> Shared Aurora DB with Replicon KMS key)
   - Flow 1: Enterprise Dedicated Flow (Enterprise Users -> API Gateway -> Business Logic -> I3 Lookup -> Dedicated Aurora DB encrypted by Customer KMS Key)

graph.name: Replicon Multi-Tenant and Dedicated Architecture with Customer-Managed Keys
graph.notes: Replicon provides time tracking and project management solutions on AWS. Standard users are onboarded into a shared multi-tenant system backed by a Shared Aurora database encrypted with Replicon's platform KMS key. Enterprise customers requiring strict compliance bring their own AWS KMS CMK key from their AWS account via key policies to encrypt dedicated Aurora databases. Routing between standard and dedicated environments is controlled dynamically by an Inter-Infrastructure Intelligence (I3) microservice running on Fargate backed by DynamoDB.

nodes.name: I3 DynamoDB Store

edges.notes: Standard users send requests through API Gateway.
API Gateway forwards requests to Business Logic compute.
Business Logic queries I3 Fargate service to look up tenant data routing location.
I3 Fargate service reads tenant lookup data from DynamoDB store.
Business Logic writes/reads multi-tenant data to Shared Aurora DB.
Replicon Platform KMS key encrypts Shared Aurora DB at rest.
Enterprise users send requests through the shared API Gateway.
API Gateway routes enterprise requests to Business Logic compute.
Business Logic queries I3 service to check destination database for enterprise customer.
I3 Fargate service retrieves dedicated enterprise metadata from DynamoDB.
Business Logic routes isolated enterprise data to Dedicated Aurora DB.
Customer KMS Key encrypts the Dedicated Aurora DB at rest.
